44711607.article_content:
A few weeks ago, Paramount, which owns CBS, announced that it would pay $16 million to settle a
laughable lawsuit
in which President Donald Trump claimed the network had committed consumer fraud by editing a pre-election interview with former Vice President Kamala Harris to make her seem "less dumb." It was a striking surrender, especially since CBS had accurately
described
Trump's claims as "completely without merit." But Brendan Carr, the Trump-appointed chairman of the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), insisted that the settlement had nothing to do with his agency's review of Paramount's pending merger with Skydance Media.
On Thursday, the FCC
announced
that it had approved that $8 billion business deal. By Carr's account, the timing of that decision was entirely coincidental. But FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez, a Joe Biden appointee, had a different take.
"I cannot support this order approving this transaction in light of the payout and other troubling concessions Paramount made to settle a baseless lawsuit," Gomez
said
in her dissent. "After months of cowardly capitulation to this Administration, Paramount finally got what it wanted. Unfortunately, it is the American public who will ultimately pay the price for its actions. In an unprecedented move, this once-independent FCC used its vast power to pressure Paramount to broker a private legal settlement and further erode press freedom."
In addition to its suspicious timing, the FCC's approval of the Paramount/Skydance deal was contingent on concessions regarding CBS news coverage. Those constitutionally questionable conditions confirm that Carr is
determined
to curb freedom of the press by asserting government control over the content of broadcast journalism.
"This has been an unconstitutional shakedown from start to finish,"
said
Will Creeley, legal director at the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression. "Per the First Amendment, federal law, and longstanding precedent, the FCC has no business dictating the editorial choices of media outlets or conditioning merger approval on the viewpoints a network chooses to air….No federal bureaucrat should ever be allowed to play-act as our nation's editor-in-chief."
Paramount needed the FCC's approval for the merger because it entailed the transfer of broadcast licenses held by CBS-owned stations. Under the
Communications Act of 1934
, the question was whether those transfers were "consistent with the public interest, convenience, and necessity." As Carr sees it, that standard requires assurances that licensees will cover the news in a way that he deems fair, accurate, and balanced.
"Americans no longer trust the legacy national news media to report fully, accurately, and fairly," Carr
said
in a press release. "It is time for a change. That is why I welcome Skydance's commitment to make significant changes at the once storied CBS broadcast network."
In particular, Carr said, "Skydance has made written commitments to ensure that the new company's programming embodies a diversity of viewpoints from across the political and ideological spectrum. Skydance will also adopt measures that can root out the bias that has undermined trust in the national news media. These commitments, if implemented, would enable CBS to operate in the public interest and focus on fair, unbiased, and fact-based coverage. Doing so would begin the process of earning back Americans' trust."
Skydance also
agreed
to "have in place an ombudsman who reports to the President of New Paramount, who will receive and evaluate any complaints of bias or other concerns involving CBS." It says "New Paramount's executive leadership will carefully consider any such complaints in overseeing CBS's news programming." Carr's press release also touted that concession, which he said will "promote transparency and increased accountability."
Carr, in other words, thinks it is entirely appropriate for federal regulators to demand "significant changes" in the way news organizations operate, including what they cover, how they cover it, the sources they interview, the people they invite to comment on current events, and the way they respond to complaints of bias. He is explicitly setting the FCC up as an arbiter of good journalism.
That power grab is consistent with Carr's
understanding
of the government's role in the marketplace of ideas, which he thinks should include
restricting
the editorial discretion of social media platforms in the name of "reining in Big Tech" and preventing "discrimination against core political viewpoints." Carr, an
avowed free speech champion
, presents his concerns about broadcast news bias in similar terms,
saying
"a handful of national programmers" should not "control and dictate to the American what the narrative is, what they can say, what they can think." As with his vendetta against "Big Tech," he perversely portrays government interference with private editorial decisions as a victory for freedom of speech.

data.title: Return of wolves to Yellowstone has led to a surge in aspen trees
data.author: geox
data.article_summary: 1995年，狼被重新引入黄石公园，此前它们因栖息地丧失、人类猎杀和政府的消灭计划而在1930年从公园消失。狼的消失导致麋鹿数量失控增长，过度啃食植被，尤其是白杨树，使得新树苗无法生长。到1990年代，黄石北部的白杨树苗几乎绝迹。狼重返公园后，麋鹿数量下降，白杨树苗开始显著恢复。研究发现，许多区域出现了多年未见的大量健康白杨树苗。虽然白杨恢复显著，但随着麋鹿数量减少，野牛数量增加，可能成为新的限制因素。狼的重新引入不仅促进了树木的恢复，还提升了整个生态系统的生物多样性，包括浆果灌木、昆虫、鸟类和海狸等物种的栖息环境。这项研究展示了顶级捕食者对生态系统的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：狼的重引入对生态系统及社会的影响

不同观点：
• **支持狼重引入及其生态影响**：
  - mkw5053 指出狼的重引入对黄石公园的生态系统产生了积极影响，例如麋鹿不再长时间停留在溪流旁，柳树和棉白杨得以生长，河狸数量增加，进而提高了水位并重建了湿地。KurSix 强调了物种之间的相互关联性，指出狼的重引入展示了生态系统中营养级联效应的实际案例。
  - thangalin 分享了一个视频链接，展示了狼如何重塑了黄石公园的生态系统。
  - arnon 简单表示这是今天的good news。

• **对狼群管理的争议**：
  - pcmaffey 强烈反对蒙大拿州提出的增加狼猎杀配额的提案，认为这是政治和利润驱动，而非科学。提案允许猎杀多达500只狼，增加了50%的猎杀量，并且每人可猎杀30只狼。pcmaffey 提出狼对维持健康猎物群体、控制慢性消耗性疾病有帮助，并指出合法狩猎可能增加偷猎行为。
  - rr808 提到当地牧场主因牲畜损失而反对狼的重引入，提出了“整体利益是否比当地居民的利益更重要”的伦理问题。

• **替代管理方案**：
  - declan_roberts 建议通过增加麋鹿标签数量来控制麋鹿数量，而不是通过猎杀狼来实现。
  - atentaten 关注狼的重引入对其他物种（如山狮）的影响，担心这是否只是在转移问题。

Wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone in 1995, over 60 years after their eradication from the national park.
(Image credit: Photo by William Campbell/Sygma via Getty Images)
Yellowstone's wolves are helping a new generation of young aspen trees to grow tall and join the forest canopy — the first new generation of such trees in Yellowstone's northern range in 80 years.
Gray wolves (
Canis lupus
)
had disappeared from Yellowstone
National Park by 1930 following extensive habitat loss, human hunting and government eradication programs. Without these top predators, populations of elk (
Cervus canadensis
) grew unfettered. At their peak population, an estimated 18,000 elk ranged across the park, chomping on grasses and shrubs as well as the leaves, twigs and bark of trees like
quaking aspen
(
Populus tremuloides
). This stopped saplings from establishing themselves, and surveys in the 1990s found no aspen saplings.
"You had older trees, and then nothing underneath,"
Luke Painter
, an ecologist at Oregon State University and lead author of the new study, told Live Science.
You may like
Instead of 'de-extincting' dire wolves, scientists should use gene editing to protect living, endangered species
Wolves help restore trees in Yellowstone and the largest interstellar object ever seen
Colossal chief scientist clarifies de-extinction claim, while confirming its 'dire wolves' are 'grey wolves with 20 edits'
But when wolves were reintroduced in 1995, the picture began to change. As wolf numbers rose, the elk population in the park dropped sharply, and it is now down to about 2,000.
In the new study, published Tuesday (July 22) in the journal
Forest Ecology and Management
, Painter and his colleagues surveyed aspen stands — specific areas of the forest where these trees grow.
Related:
Reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone helped entire ecosystem thrive, 20-year study finds
The team returned to
three areas surveyed in 2012
to examine changes to aspen sapling numbers. Of the 87 aspen stands studied, a third had a large number of tall aspen saplings throughout, indicating the trees are healthy and growing. Another third of the stands had patches of tall saplings.

"We're seeing significant new growth of young aspen and this is the first time that we've found it in our plots," Painter said. These are young aspen with a trunk greater than 2 inches (5 centimetres) in diameter at chest height — which haven't been seen there since the 1940s, he added.
"It doesn't mean that they're not going to get killed or die from something, but it's a pretty good indication that we're getting some new trees," Painter noted. "As they get bigger, they get more resilient."
Such trees are old enough to spread themselves, either by sending up new shoots from their roots a fair distance from the main tree, or via seed production, he said.
The researchers found tall aspen saplings in many of the sites studied.
(Image credit: Photo provided by Luke Painter, OSU College of Agricultural Sciences.)
However, while Yellowstone's quaking aspen are recovering, they aren't out of the woods just yet. The elk population has declined, but bison (
Bison bison
) numbers have increased in some areas in recent years.
Bison are a lot harder for wolves to take down
, said Painter, so increasing numbers of bison may be emerging as a new constraint on aspen in some areas.
Painter said that the variation in aspen recovery shows the effects of reintroducing a big predator to the top of the food chain, rather than to changes in the overall climate, for example.
The re-emergence of aspen has widespread effects, he told Live Science. "Aspen are a key species for biodiversity. The canopy is more open than it is with conifers and you get filtering light that creates a habitat that supports a lot of diversity of plants."
This means a boost to berry-producing shrubs, insects and birds and also species like beavers, because
the trees are a preferred food and building material for the semi- aquatic rodents
, along with the willows and cottonwoods that grow near to water in the region.

There are also hints that the number of bears and cougars in the region have increased since wolves were introduced, Painter said, but it's not clear why.

44658323.article_summary: 1995年，狼被重新引入黄石公园，此前它们因栖息地丧失、人类猎杀和政府的消灭计划而在1930年从公园消失。狼的消失导致麋鹿数量失控增长，过度啃食植被，尤其是白杨树，使得新树苗无法生长。到1990年代，黄石北部的白杨树苗几乎绝迹。狼重返公园后，麋鹿数量下降，白杨树苗开始显著恢复。研究发现，许多区域出现了多年未见的大量健康白杨树苗。虽然白杨恢复显著，但随着麋鹿数量减少，野牛数量增加，可能成为新的限制因素。狼的重新引入不仅促进了树木的恢复，还提升了整个生态系统的生物多样性，包括浆果灌木、昆虫、鸟类和海狸等物种的栖息环境。这项研究展示了顶级捕食者对生态系统的重要性。

data.title: 4k NASA employees opt to leave agency through deferred resignation program
data.author: ProAm
data.article_summary: 近4,000名NASA员工选择通过延迟辞职计划离开该机构，约占NASA员工总数的20%，使员工人数从18,000减至14,000。这一计划是特朗普政府为缩减联邦政府 workforce 推出的，此外还提议将NASA的预算削减约24%。不过，近期通过的《One Big Beautiful Bill Act》为NASA在2032年前额外拨款近100亿美元，支持火星任务和重返月球计划。NASA的预算和裁员计划遭到科学家和太空组织的批评，300多名现任和前任NASA员工联名致信，反对这些削减计划。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NASA预算削减及其影响，尤其是科学任务和人员被裁减的问题，以及与SLS等项目的低效对比。

不同观点：
• **支持科学任务的观点**：[gammarator]、[ericvolp12]、[rockskon]认为，NASA削减了极具生产力的科学任务，导致大量专家流失，特别是在天体物理学和深空探测领域。这些领域的人才在私营部门没有对应的机会，因此他们的失业将对美国科学研究产生长期负面影响。

• **支持改革和精简的观点**：[eagerpace]、[bradley13]认为，NASA需要改革，尽管当前的改革方式可能导致人才流失和不确定性，但从长远来看，可能带来新的思维方式和改进。SLS项目被认为是低效的，应该被重新审视。

• **批评当前改革方式的观点**：[samrus]、[yalogin]认为，当前的削减是政治操作，旨在通过削弱联邦机构来推动私有化，最终会导致美国在科学领域的领导地位下降，并对公共卫生和国家安全等领域产生长期负面影响。

• **关注具体实施和影响的观点**：[cozzyd]、[mosesbp]关注削减预算对具体项目和人员的影响，特别是涉及到的承包商和科研人员的去向问题。他们担心关键项目的延误和科研人员的流失。

• **建议改革NASA运营模式的观点**：[BobbyJo]建议，NASA需要一个更明确、可衡量的使命，类似于联邦储备的简单明确目标，以便公众和代表能够对NASA进行有效监督，避免成为政治利益的牺牲品。

• **关注人员构成和再就业的观点**：[hk1337]、[_carbyau_]、[tonyhart7]关注NASA内部人员构成，特别是工程师与管理人员的比例，以及被裁人员再就业的可能性，希望私营航天公司能够吸纳这些专业人才。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于NASA当前的预算削减是否合理，特别是科学任务的取消和对SLS等项目的持续投资是否符合长远利益。
• 私营部门在科学研究中的角色也被提及，强调SpaceX等公司不进行基础科学研究，无法填补NASA科学任务被削减带来的空白。
• 讨论还涉及联邦机构的改革和私有化问题，部分评论认为当前的改革是短视的资本运作，将对国家长期发展不利。

44699052.article_content:
NPR
Nearly 4,000 NASA employees opt to leave agency through deferred resignation program
Chandelis Duster
Jul. 26, 2025
MORE
Workers on scaffolding repaint the NASA logo near the top of the Vehicle Assembly Building at the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Fla., May 2020.
Photo by
John Raoux
-
AP
Nearly 4,000 NASA employees have opted to leave the space agency through the Trump administration's deferred resignation program, NASA said on Saturday.
The cuts amount to an estimated 20% of NASA's workforce, and will reduce the agency from 18,000 to 14,000 employees, NASA spokesperson Cheryl Warner said in a statement shared with NPR. The total number includes the agency's loss of 500 other workers due to normal attrition, she said.
During a second round of the program, which closed at midnight Friday, 3,000 employees applied to leave the agency, Warner said, following the 870 employees that applied to leave during the first round.
The resignations follow the Trump administration's plan to reduce the federal workforce and implement cuts recommended by the
Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE)
.
NPR has reached out to the White House for comment.
It's unclear when the full reduction of the workforce will take effect, Warner said. NASA did not respond to NPR's questions about how the workforce cuts will affect the agency.
The administration has also proposed
decreasing NASA's budget
. A fiscal year 2026
budget request
released in May would reduce funding for the agency by about 24% (from nearly $25 billion to nearly $19 billion.) But the
House
and
Senate
are discussing recommendations that would keep funding for the agency around the current budget.
Concerning funding beyond the next fiscal year, however, the agency recently got a boost — reversing earlier proposals to retire some NASA programs. Trump's
One Big Beautiful Bill Act
that he signed into law earlier this month, allocates nearly $10 billion in additional funding for NASA through 2032, including backing for Mars missions and plans to return to the moon.
The White House's proposed budget cuts and changes at the agency have faced criticism from scientists and space organizations, including The Planetary Society, a nonprofit led by Bill Nye, "The Science Guy."
"The Planetary Society believes that a great nation deserves a great space program, one that reflects our national ideals and serves the public interest," the organization said about the White House budget proposal in May. "This proposal doesn't merely fall short — it actively rejects that promise, undermining the rare opportunity NASA provides to build unity at home and collaboration abroad through American leadership."
On Monday, more than 300 current and former NASA employees signed and sent a
letter
known as the "Voyager Declaration" to interim NASA administrator Sean Duffy, criticizing "rapid and wasteful changes" at the agency that they say include cuts to programs and research. They also urged Duffy to not implement the proposed cuts and said "they are not in the best interest of NASA."

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：QR码和数据恢复中的错误纠正技术及其应用

不同观点：
• [eknkc] 分享了20年前从Usenet下载数据时使用par文件进行错误纠正的经历。他提到文件被分割成块，若某块丢失或损坏，par文件可以帮助恢复，且无需下载整个par文件，只需下载对应缺失部分即可。他还表示对错误纠正（如Reed-Solomon算法）的原理非常感兴趣，甚至自己尝试实现了一个简单的版本。

• [dunconian] 讲述了自己在工作中处理不可扫描的QR码的经历。他通过手动解码QR码，发现是错误纠正模式中的一个错误导致信息长度位被翻转，从而导致不同扫描器出现不同问题（如返回垃圾数据、崩溃或返回上次扫描的结果）。这个经历让他深入了解了Reed-Solomon错误纠正的实际应用。

• [Theodores] 对QR码的美学设计提出了问题，比如边框大小规则以及如何在QR码中添加Logo。他还讨论了在不同大小的QR码（如21x21模块）中如何选择优化方案，并询问是否"块状"设计最优。

补充讨论：
• [cinntaile] 提到该内容在三天前已经被重新提交，暗示可能存在重复讨论的问题，这与内容的时效性和社区的讨论管理有关。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户关注的角度不同：[eknkc] 和 [dunconian] 更关注错误纠正技术的实现和原理，而 [Theodores] 则关心QR码的设计和优化问题。这两方面在实际应用中可能需要权衡。

• 对于QR码设计和错误纠正的优先级存在潜在讨论空间：美观和功能性之间的平衡，以及不同场景下QR码的最优大小和设计选择。

补充讨论：
• [cinntaile] 提到该内容在三天前已经被重新提交，暗示可能存在重复讨论的问题，这与内容的时效性和社区的讨论管理有关。

争议焦点：
• 不同用户关注的角度不同：[eknkc] 和 [dunconian] 更关注错误纠正技术的实现和原理，而 [Theodores] 则关心QR码的设计和优化问题。这两方面在实际应用中可能需要权衡。

• 对于QR码设计和错误纠正的优先级存在潜在讨论空间：美观和功能性之间的平衡，以及不同场景下QR码的最优大小和设计选择。

Porn sites may have blown up Meta's key defense in a copyright fight with book authors who earlier this year
said that Meta torrented
"at least 81.7 terabytes of data across multiple shadow libraries" to train its AI models.
Meta has defeated most of the authors' claims and claimed there is no proof that Meta ever uploaded pirated data through seeding or leeching on the BitTorrent network used to download training data. But authors
still have a chance to prove that Meta may have profited
off its massive piracy, and a new
lawsuit
filed by adult sites last week appears to contain evidence that could help authors win their fight, TorrentFreak
reported
.
The new lawsuit was filed last Friday in a US district court in California by Strike 3 Holdings—which says it attracts "over 25 million monthly visitors" to sites that serve as "ethical sources" for adult videos that "are famous for redefining adult content with Hollywood style and quality."
After authors revealed Meta's torrenting, Strike 3 Holdings checked its proprietary BitTorrent-tracking tools designed to detect infringement of its videos and alleged that the company found evidence that Meta has been torrenting and seeding its copyrighted content for years—since at least 2018. Some of the IP addresses were clearly registered to Meta, while others appeared to be "hidden," and at least one was linked to a Meta employee, the filing said.
Meta’s AI training tactics may have harmed minors
According to Strike 3 Holdings, Meta "willfully and intentionally" infringed "at least 2,396 movies" as part of a strategy to download terabytes of data as fast as possible by seeding popular high-quality porn. Supposedly, Meta continued seeding the content "sometimes for days, weeks, or even months" after downloading them, and these movies may also have been secretly used to train Meta's AI models, Strike 3 Holdings alleged.
The porn site operator explained to the court that BitTorrent's protocol establishes a "tit-for-tat" mechanism that "rewards users who distribute the most desired content." It alleged that Meta took advantage of this system by "often" pirating adult videos that are "often within the most infringed files on BitTorrent websites" on "the very same day the motion pictures are released."
These tactics allegedly gave Meta several advantages, making it harder for Strike 3 Holdings' sites to compete, including potentially distributing the videos to minors for free without age checks in states that now require them.
"Meta specifically targeted Plaintiffs’ content for distribution in order to accelerate its downloads of vast amounts of other content," the lawsuit said. And while Meta claimed that it "wrote a script to intentionally limit distributing popular books on BitTorrent," Strike 3 Holdings believes "discovery will likely show" Meta "continuously" distributed its adult videos specifically as a strategy to get around the BitTorrent protocol.
So far, Strike 3 Holdings says it has documented at least five episodes in which Meta "hand-picked" adult videos from a specific site for "intense periods of distribution" to avoid seeding other content it was sourcing through BitTorrent.
"The only reason to incur the server and bandwidth expense of remaining in a swarm for these long durations is to leverage the extended distribution as tit-for-tat currency in order to efficiently download millions of other files from BitTorrent," Strike 3 Holdings alleged.
Strike 3 Holdings is seeking extensive damages and an injunction to permanently stop Meta from pirating its videos.
The company also wants Meta to delete any stolen videos from its AI training data and existing AI models. The company alleged that Meta could use its high-quality copyrighted works—which provide rare long cuts of "natural, human-centric imagery" showing "parts of the body not found in regular videos" and "unique" forms "of human interactions and facial expressions"—to create a rival adult video generator that could "eventually create identical content for little to no cost."
"Plaintiffs cannot compete against Meta when it ignores federal and state laws and offers Plaintiffs’ works for free," Strike 3 Holdings alleged. "This will effectively eliminate Plaintiffs’ future ability to compete in the marketplace" as well as its brands' "hard-earned reputations as respected and ethical sources for high-quality adult motion pictures by potentially allowing minors unfettered access to Plaintiffs’ content against Plaintiffs’ consent."
Ars could not immediately reach Meta, Strike 3 Holdings' in-house lawyer, or book authors' lawyers for comment.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：去中心化应用（dapps）的现状及未来趋势

不同观点：
• mathattack 认为目前去中心化应用（dapps）领域存在大量的低质量项目，许多项目只是简单复制已有功能，缺乏创新。这导致市场充斥着许多不可靠的项目，尤其是一些交易量超过百万美元的dapps，实际上并没有提供独特的价值。

• mouse_ 指出，随着市场流动性下降，dapps为了维持运营可能会增加杠杆和交易量，但这并不是一个好的趋势。同时，他也预期市场将会出现整合（consolidation），即许多功能相似的dapps会被淘汰或合并，最终留下更少但更具竞争力的项目。

补充讨论：
• mathattack 提到了“低门槛”的问题，认为这使得创建dapps变得过于容易，从而导致大量低质量的项目涌现。这可能是市场不成熟的一个表现。

• mouse_ 强调了流动性和杠杆的问题，认为流动性的下降可能会迫使dapps采取一些冒险的策略，如增加杠杆和交易量，这可能会进一步增加市场的风险。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于dapps市场的未来发展趋势。mathattack 对当前市场的低质量项目表示担忧，而 mouse_ 则更关注流动性下降带来的潜在风险和市场整合的可能性。两者都认为当前市场存在问题，但关注的方面有所不同。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是关于市场整合的预期。mouse_ 认为市场将会出现整合，而 mathattack 并没有直接提及这一点，但其对低质量项目的批评间接支持了这一预期。

总结：
当前dapps市场面临着项目质量参差不齐、流动性下降以及潜在的市场整合等问题。不同观点主要集中在问题的具体表现和未来趋势的预期上。

data.title: I Got Claude to Write Code I Could Ship
data.author: gen220
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何使用Anthropic的Claude Code工具来编写可交付的代码。尽管Claude Code能自动化处理许多任务，如修复bug和重构代码，但它生成的代码往往过于庞大且难以理解，导致审查困难。为解决这一问题，作者引入了"stacked PRs"（堆叠式拉取请求）的方法，将大块代码拆分为一系列小而可独立审查的PRs。通过在提示中加入规划和分步执行的指导，Claude Code学会了按计划生成堆叠的PRs，从而提高了代码的可审查性和质量。最终，Claude Code成为作者处理工程任务的得力工具，尤其在处理遗留代码和长期搁置的重构任务方面表现出色。作者还开发了GT MCP工具，以推广这种工作流并应用于其他AI代理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：代码提交的结构和流程优化

不同观点：
• frankfrank13指出，当前堆栈中最大的Pull Request（PR）包含268行代码，但大部分是HTML。这表明该PR的主要内容为HTML结构和样式，可能相对简单。该用户关注代码的组成以及每部分的贡献。

• frankfrank13建议在编写任何代码之前，应向用户展示计划提交的堆栈结构，并请求确认。这强调了在开发过程中透明度和用户确认的重要性，以确保开发方向符合预期。

• 该用户还强调了每个PR的代码必须是原子的（即单一职责，不包含不相关更改），并且必须通过持续集成（CI）。这指出了代码质量和开发流程中的关键要求，以确保每个PR的独立性和稳定性。

补充讨论：
• 强调了在PR提交之前，确认代码结构和通过CI的重要性，以避免不必要的错误和回滚。
• 提出了对代码提交流程的改进建议，特别是在多层审核和确认机制方面，以提高团队协作的效率和代码质量。

争议焦点：
• 当前堆栈中PR的大小和内容构成是否合理。有人可能认为268行的HTML代码是可以接受的，而其他人可能觉得应该进一步拆分以提高可读性和审核效率。
• 如何在代码提交前有效地进行结构展示和确认，以平衡开发速度和代码质量。这可能涉及工具支持和团队流程的调整。

44711199.article_content:
Engineering
Launches
Stacking
How I got Claude to write code I could actually ship
July 25, 2025
Last week, Anthropic released a statement showing that Claude Code
usage has increased by 300%
in the last 3 months. The appeal of Claude Code is obvious; every team has a laundry list of tasks that are nice-to-have but never make it over the cut line. You know the drill:
Refactor that brittle module I’ve been side-eyeing since early-2024.
Clean up some interfaces that scream “we rushed this out to hit the deadline, and have been scared to touch it ever since.”
Write tests.
Proponents claim that Claude Code can now automate all of this work. If this were true, it would change a lot of things. So, I figured we had to try it out for ourselves.
Testing Claude Code’s abilities
I started with something small: identifying the cause of a bug that was triggering off-by-one errors under very specific edge cases on the Graphite dashboard. After reticulating for a minute or so Claude, impressively, returned a concise summary of the problem, the offending change that regressed this behavior (spoiler: it was me) and staged a fix.
Emboldened by this success, I moved on to having Claude perform a refactor in some well tested code that I’d been putting off. It confidently responded with a few thousand lines of code—an unreadable mess that would take hours to carefully review. Worse, Claude had modified the test files, too. Though the PR was “green,” I was no longer sure it was safe to land.
It turns out this was a theme. Trying to vibe code even medium‑complexity features was proving difficult—not because writing the code was hard, but because it was too easy. It was too easy to create thousands of lines of code where even you as the author have no idea how it works. When that code makes it to review, your only option is to “LGTM” and pray, which isn't really an option in any serious engineering org. For many engineers on our team, this tradeoff meant that they were either using Claude Code for point fixes or not at all.
AI-generated code needs stacked PRs
Large PRs are not a novel problem.
Studies show
that only 24% of large PRs (>1000 lines) receive
any
review comments. AI only exacerbates this by producing far more code than humans do. And let’s face it, that code often fails to capture the intent of the person who prompted it.
The solution to this problem, for humans, is something we at Graphite know a thing or two about—
stacked diffs
. Instead of a single, large PR that implements an entire feature, engineers can put up a sequence of smaller PRs in a “stack” that keeps each change focused and easily reviewable.
This got me wondering, “Could we teach Claude to stack?”
Teaching Claude to stack
I started by adding instructions that explained stacking and how to use the
gt
CLI to our monorepo’s
CLAUDE.md
file:
With this new prompt, Claude started using
gt
to
create stacks of PRs
, but the boundaries between them were messy. Tests were added before their dependencies existed, and a refactor was split across multiple PRs, leaving none able to pass CI.
I realized that stacking is about more than just writing “small PRs.” It forces you to think critically about the work you intend to do, so you can build a clear plan and share it meaningfully with reviewers. The PRs were small, but they didn’t build and were hard to understand. Turns out, stacking like a senior engineer takes planning, which Claude wasn’t doing on its own, so we need to teach it that too.
Before I create a stack myself, I like to think about where the feature is going and the building blocks that will be needed to get there. For example: I might start by defining interfaces, then the server logic, and finally the frontend UX.
This maps cleanly to the concept of “Todos” in Claude Code, which is the mechanism that the agent uses internally to plan out complex tasks. I added this to Claude’s instructions:
With a few more tweaks to the instructions, Claude Code started organizing its “Todos” as a stack—one pull request for each task. Check out this example, where I asked Claude to build a
Wordle
app:
And voilà! Claude Code built Wordle, as a stack of pull requests:
#1 feat: add basic HTML structure and styling for Wordle game
+268/-0
#2 feat: implement core game logic and state management
+129/-2
#3 feat: add keyboard input handling
+29/-1
#4 feat: add animations and visual feedback
+33/-4
Each PR focuses on a different area of the project, and can be independently reviewed.
Building with Claude Code and GT MCP
Claude Code has become my go-to tool for getting real engineering work done—building features, cleaning up legacy code, and finally tackling the long list of refactors I’d been putting off. It works well because it plans the way engineers do: breaking things down into smaller, reviewable steps. We built the
GT MCP
to capture this workflow and make it so any agent can follow stacking best practices.
The GT MCP allows AI agents to automatically generate stacked
44711199.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何使用Anthropic的Claude Code工具来编写可交付的代码。尽管Claude Code能自动化处理许多任务，如修复bug和重构代码，但它生成的代码往往过于庞大且难以理解，导致审查困难。为解决这一问题，作者引入了"stacked PRs"（堆叠式拉取请求）的方法，将大块代码拆分为一系列小而可独立审查的PRs。通过在提示中加入规划和分步执行的指导，Claude Code学会了按计划生成堆叠的PRs，从而提高了代码的可审查性和质量。最终，Claude Code成为作者处理工程任务的得力工具，尤其在处理遗留代码和长期搁置的重构任务方面表现出色。作者还开发了GT MCP工具，以推广这种工作流并应用于其他AI代理。

主要讨论点：代码提交的结构和流程优化

不同观点：
• frankfrank13指出，当前堆栈中最大的Pull Request（PR）包含268行代码，但大部分是HTML。这表明该PR的主要内容为HTML结构和样式，可能相对简单。该用户关注代码的组成以及每部分的贡献。

• frankfrank13建议在编写任何代码之前，应向用户展示计划提交的堆栈结构，并请求确认。这强调了在开发过程中透明度和用户确认的重要性，以确保开发方向符合预期。

• 该用户还强调了每个PR的代码必须是原子的（即单一职责，不包含不相关更改），并且必须通过持续集成（CI）。这指出了代码质量和开发流程中的关键要求，以确保每个PR的独立性和稳定性。

补充讨论：
• 强调了在PR提交之前，确认代码结构和通过CI的重要性，以避免不必要的错误和回滚。
• 提出了对代码提交流程的改进建议，特别是在多层审核和确认机制方面，以提高团队协作的效率和代码质量。

争议焦点：
• 当前堆栈中PR的大小和内容构成是否合理。有人可能认为268行的HTML代码是可以接受的，而其他人可能觉得应该进一步拆分以提高可读性和审核效率。
• 如何在代码提交前有效地进行结构展示和确认，以平衡开发速度和代码质量。这可能涉及工具支持和团队流程的调整。

data.title: When photography was born, fascination, obsession, and danger followed
data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：摄影技术的发展、其与艺术的关系以及与现代AI技术的类比

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun分享了个人作为“摄影系谱学家”的经历，讲述了家族照片收集和分析的过程。他强调了摄影技术从早期锡版照片到柯达布朗尼相机，再到彩色照片的发展历程，并对不同阶段的照片质量进行了评价。他认为彩色照片在某些阶段的质量不如黑白照片，并对技术革新带来的质量变化表示感慨。

• api将摄影技术的发展与当前AI和艺术的讨论进行了类比，指出两者在道德恐慌和公众讨论上的相似性。他提到历史上对摄影的道德批评，特别是其在色情内容制作中的应用，并认为这些讨论与当前AI生成内容的争议非常相似。

• chazeon通过参观宾夕法尼亚铁路博物馆的经历，将早期铁路技术与当前AI技术的发展进行了类比，指出人们对新技术的恐惧和抵制是一种常见现象。

• k__认为摄影写实主义只是表面上的真实，任何技术娴熟的摄影师都知道这并非事实。他将此与LLM生成的文本进行比较，指出两者都具有类似的表面真实性。

• echelon将早期摄影技术的批评与当前生成式AI的批评进行了对比，指出尽管摄影技术发展过程中存在诸多问题和争议，但最终其积极影响超过了负面影响。他引用了Susan Sontag等人的观点，强调了摄影技术对文化和社会的影响。

• 75345d4c持有激进观点，认为化学感光摄影技术永远不能算作真正的艺术，主张委托画家进行创作。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于摄影技术是否能被视为艺术，以及新技术（如AI生成内容）在艺术领域的地位和影响。
• JKCalhoun通过具体例子展示了摄影技术发展的不同阶段及其对照片质量的影响，提供了历史发展的实证支持。
• api和echelon都将历史上的摄影技术争议与当前AI技术的讨论进行了类比，强调了技术发展过程中相似的心理和社会反应。
• 75345d4c的观点较为极端，认为传统绘画才是真正的艺术，对摄影和AI技术持否定态度。

data.title: Claude Code is a slot machine
data.author: rgoldfinger
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了AI工具对软件工程师工作的影响。作者最初因为热爱编程过程——将想法变为现实的乐趣——而成为工程师。然而，AI工具的引入打破了这种“心流”体验，编程变得更多是间歇性的奖励和等待。作者引用了两种工作模式：“魔法师”模式，快速创造但不深入；以及“书记员”模式，深入理解每个细节。真正的技能在于知道何时使用哪种模式，并在两者间灵活切换。AI工具可以加速创建过程，但最终仍需深入细节才能确保其正常工作。文章还提到，AI工具的流行部分源于类似老虎机的间歇奖励效应，吸引人们不断尝试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码工具（如Claude Code）对软件工程的影响及使用体验

不同观点：
• Wowfunhappy：认为AI编码工具（如Claude Code）能帮助处理繁琐的细节工作，使得编码过程更加有趣和高效。尽管AI无法完全替代人工，但在解决技术问题和迭代测试方面表现突出。
• jonator：强调AI工具帮助加速了从构思到产品实现的过程，减少了繁琐的决策过程，同时提高了输出质量。尽管对AI的社会影响有疑虑，但认可其在软件开发中的巨大价值。
• tptacek：指出大部分编程工作是机械重复的，应该被自动化。AI工具的出现有助于解放程序员，让他们专注于更有趣和创新的工作。
• kregasaurusrex：分享了AI工具在处理复杂问题时的局限性，例如在处理特定语言或库的兼容性问题时可能效率不高，导致时间和成本的浪费。
• b_e_n_t_o_n：认为AI应被视为一种工具，而不是万能解决方案。AI在某些情况下非常有用，但滥用可能导致挫败感。
• eric-burel：批评了关于LLM开发的低质量讨论，认为专业领域应该有更高质量的讨论和资源。
• quatonion：作为有多年经验的程序员，享受AI工具带来的新鲜体验和高效生产力，尽管需要一些指导和帮助。
• ryanegt：承认AI工具在处理重复性工作中的价值，但强调AI只有在良好的代码基础上才能发挥最大作用，程序员需要适应和学习新工具。
• scoreandmore：指出AI工具使用过程中可能导致的“上瘾”现象，类似于赌博，需要自我控制。
• stillpointlab：描述了与AI工具合作的独特体验，尽管需要频繁修正和调整，但总体上提高了工作效率和代码质量。
• jgb1984：批评AI生成的代码质量低下，认为这会导致软件质量下降，行业面临风险。
• gonzalohm：分享了AI在处理复杂规则时的局限性，认为AI在某些情况下无法提供有效的帮助。
• ChuckMcM：将LLM的使用比喻为“老虎机”，有时能带来巨大收益，但也存在风险。
• dmh2000：作为年长程序员，认为AI工具延长了其职业生涯，帮助应对因年龄导致的专注力下降。

补充讨论：
• AI工具在软件开发中的潜力和局限性：一些用户认为AI能显著提高生产力和代码质量，而另一些用户则指出其在处理复杂问题和特定语言或库时的局限性。
• 对AI工具的依赖和“上瘾”现象：有用户担心过度依赖AI工具可能导致效率低下和挫败感，类似于赌博行为。
• 对软件行业和社会的影响：部分用户关注AI工具对软件行业质量的影响，以及其在社会层面的潜在影响。
• 适应和学习新工具的必要性：许多用户强调程序员需要适应和学习如何有效使用AI工具，以保持竞争力。

44702046.article_content:
...but the odds are better
Claude Code keeps me waiting. Here I am pressing return like a crack-addicted rodent in a lab. âYes, I want to make this edit.â I watch as it works, glassy-eyed and bored as the code scrolls by, and on the edge of my seat because my ideas are about to become reality.
I became a software engineer because I loved the process of it. I could sit for hours, figuring out how to wire something up
just so
and get an idea made into something real. And it didnât feel like work. It was just fun. Joyful. Satisfying.
AI disrupts the process. What was that high from flow state is now intermittent rewards and a lot of waiting. And maybe that's ok. Maybe that's the new skill. Iâm in meetings all day anyways.
Software engineering is all about managing complexity. Early on in my career, someone much wiser than me described two modes of operating: the Conjurer, and the Scribe. The Conjurer is a wizard, creating realities out of thin air, working in broad strokes and never going deep. The Scribe reads every line of the text, and every line it refers to, understanding everything to its deepest and fullest extent before acting. Some of us tend more towards one way of operating or the other. Both are critical.
But the real skill, the real thing that makes you effective, is knowing when to use one mode or the other, and being able to switch between them as needed. When does understanding matter? When should we skip it and move onto the next thing? In a field with endless and important detail at every level, we have to both âlet it go and move onâ and âslow downâ constantly.
AI coding tools supercharge this, allowing you to bring whole machineries to life by waving your hands around, offloading the understanding for much longer, but if you want it all to actually
work
, you'll need to dive into the details eventually.
I'm guessing that part of why AI coding tools are so popular is the slot machine effect. Intermittent rewards, lots of waiting that fractures your attention, and inherent laziness keeping you trying with yet another prompt in hopes that you donât have to actually turn on your brain after so many hours of being told not to.
The exhilarating power of creation. Just insert a few more cents, and youâll get another shot at making your dreams a reality.
July 26, 2025
Â·
Roger Goldfinger

data.title: Linux on Snapdragon X Elite: Linaro and Tuxedo Pave the Way for ARM64 Laptops
data.author: MarcusE1W
data.article_summary: 在2025年Linaro Connect大会上，Linaro和TUXEDO Computers展示了采用Snapdragon X Elite SoC的ARM64 Linux笔记本原型，标志着Linux对Snapdragon设备支持的显著进展。尽管这些设备主要支持Windows on Arm，但通过Qualcomm、Linaro及社区的合作，Linux内核已支持包括Lenovo、Dell、HP等多款Snapdragon笔记本。当前进展包括GPU加速、外接显示、音频、摄像头、Wi-Fi等功能的支持。尽管Linux在ARM64笔记本上的体验仍落后于Windows和x86笔记本，但Ubuntu和Fedora等发行版正积极增加支持。TUXEDO Computers承诺推出预装Linux的Qualcomm笔记本，进一步推动Linux在ARM架构设备上的应用，为用户提供更多选择和创新机会。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux在商用笔记本上的支持情况、Tuxedo笔记本的硬件与软件问题、移动设备上的Linux与虚拟化支持。

不同观点：
• **Tuxedo笔记本的批评**：[pentamassiv] 提到Tuxedo笔记本未能兑现对fwupd、上游驱动和coreboot的支持承诺，内核开发者甚至考虑将其列入黑名单。此外，Tuxedo的设备设置需要依赖其Electron应用，体验不佳，且设备不可自行修理。
• **对移动Linux设备现状的不满**：[fb03] 表达了对当前移动Linux设备（尤其是Ubuntu）在电池续航和性能上的失望，认为苹果设备尽管封闭但表现更好。同时批评了Snapdragon上的软件进展缓慢。
• **对Surface支持的质疑**：[shenki0] 指出微软Surface Laptop 7的触摸板和触摸屏不支持，质疑其是否真的“支持”Linux。
• **对低功耗Linux笔记本的需求**：[rr808] 表示希望摆脱Windows和苹果生态，但目前可选的Linux笔记本不多，对高续航低功耗的Linux笔记本有强烈需求。
• **对商用笔记本Linux支持的体验**：[teo_zero] 提到当前Linux内核已经支持许多商用笔记本型号，询问其他用户的使用体验。

补充讨论：
• **Linux在ARM设备上的潜力与挑战**：[diabllicseagull] 认为Linux在ARM设备上有很大潜力，但电源管理和固件支持仍是主要问题。

At Linaro Connect 2025 Linaro, thanks to its work within the Qualcomm ecosystem, and TUXEDO Computers, showcased an off-the-shelf prototype ARM64 Linux laptop using the Snapdragon X Elite SoC, demonstrating progress in enabling Linux on Snapdragon devices to meet the increasing demand for ARM computing.
But wait! This is just the tip of the iceberg of a long journey!
Advancements in Linux Support for Snapdragon X Elite:
Over the past year, substantial progress has been made in integrating Linux support for Snapdragon X Elite laptops.
Qualcomm and many laptop vendors worked together to bring to market a new family of Snapdragon-powered personal computers. This new processor family ticks all the boxes for powerful and productive machines, and the collaboration with Microsoft brought the support for Windows on Arm on these devices as the main operating system (which Linaro has
contributed to as well
).
Unfortunately, like Apple computers, there is no native out-of-the-box Linux support.
The effort from Qualcomm and Linaro has been crucial to bring a functional Linux to the new family of ARM64-powered laptops.
The engineering experts from Qualcomm, Linaro and the kernel community have made a stable Linux experience possible across many Qualcomm processors, including the newer Snapdragon X Elite.
But we are still missing pre-installed Linux laptops. In the x86 processor-based laptop market, many vendors now offer Linux options.
State of the art:
Where are we now with the Linux support on these Snapdragon laptops?
A year after the processor announcement, the current Linux Kernel 6.15 already supports many commercial laptops:
Lenovo Yoga 7x
Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6
Dell XPS 13
Asus Vivobook S15
HP Omnibook x14
Microsoft Surface 13/15
The enablement wouldn’t have been possible without the collaboration between Linaro, Qualcomm, the community, and the laptop vendors.
During the last few years, Linaro engineers have contributed to many improvements in terms of functionalities and use cases, including:
GPU and 2D/3D acceleration
External display output (USB-C DP altmode)
USB enablement
Audio support
Software camera support
Thermal management
Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/Modem
Suspend/resume
Contact Us
to know more.
Currently, the Linux experience on ARM64 laptops lags behind Windows on the same hardware and Linux on x86 laptops. Linaro’s goal is to enhance the out-of-the-box experience, reliability, and overall user experience on Qualcomm-powered laptops running popular Linux distributions, such as Debian and Fedora, by addressing fundamental issues.
Watch the Linux ARM64 Compute Laptops BoF discussion at Linaro Connect 2025
Thanks to the changes available in the kernel, Ubuntu community has released an installable Concept Distro for Ubuntu 24.10 and now Canonical is adding ARM64 Laptops
support for Ubuntu 25.04 distro
and also
Fedora is working on it
.
In other words, the development progress is going in the right direction, distro support is on its way and many people are starting to drive these devices with Linux daily.
TUXEDO Computers’ Commitment to Linux on ARM:
The integration of Linux on Qualcomm laptops signifies more than just a technical milestone. It has the potential to create a positive impact on the global technology ecosystem and the wider market.
This is what the folks at
TUXEDO Computers
are putting their bets on, a full-fledged laptop with one of the latest and innovative ARM64 processors with Linux. The promise and the commitment from TUXEDO to release a Qualcomm Laptop with pre-installed Linux is a living fact that this operating system is mature enough for desktop use on these devices.
Tuxedo directly contacted us for help for technical support to bring up the missing bits on the device, and they sent us two prototypes to develop on. Collaboration between experts from both companies successfully enabled Linux installation and the proper functioning of many features on this device.
The unique nature of this case study and its growing interest create new opportunities for developers, businesses, and consumers who require Linux in their Snapdragon X Series family products, paving the way for increased choice and innovation in the ARM64-based laptop space and beyond.

While we are still in the development phase, we can confidently say that users can look forward to long battery

data.title: I designed my own fast game streaming video codec – PyroWave
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了通过网络在两台机器间低延迟传输游戏画面的技术需求和挑战，强调每一毫秒的延迟都很关键。整个过程包括从机器A发送控制输入到机器B，B渲染帧、编码并传输，最后机器A解码并显示图像。为实现低延迟，通常使用GPU加速的视频压缩，如H.264、HEVC或AV1。为了进一步减少延迟，可以采取以下策略：

1. **仅使用帧内编码**：抛弃运动预测以提高错误恢复能力和简化编码过程，代价是比特率大幅增加。
2. **抛弃熵编码**：熵编码不利于并行化，去除它可以加速编码。
3. **离散小波变换**：尽管现代编码多用离散余弦变换（DCT），但小波变换在某些特定领域仍有应用价值。

这些方法可以实现超低延迟，但代价是更高的带宽消耗，适合本地局域网内使用，而不适合互联网传输。文章还提到了专业广播领域和特定硬件实现的例子。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：视频编码的低延迟与高效压缩技术，尤其是在游戏流媒体和研究项目中的应用。

不同观点：
• Thaxll提到VLC创建者正在开发类似的尖端低延迟流媒体技术，并分享了相关采访和视频链接。
• Sippeangelo认为，如果编码器与游戏引擎合作，比如利用运动预测，游戏流媒体的性能可以大幅提升，但可能受到专利的限制。
• Raphman指出JPEG-XS标准也是一个低延迟的选项，尤其适合商业项目，因为有专利池保护。
• Keketi提出使用LLM（大型语言模型）进行游戏画面文本转录和重建的创意，尽管有损且慢，但压缩比极高。
• Cadwhisker提到该编解码器使用与HTJ2K相同的算法，并希望了解两者之间的差异。
• Monster_truck认为该技术类似于NDI，但缺乏NDI的便利性，并提到使用nvenc的超低延迟预设。
• CharlesW建议与H.264/AVC进行基准测试对比，并提供了ffmpeg设置示例。
• Kookamamie认为最接近的竞争者是NDI，由Vizrt（前NewTek）推出，目标是类似的比特率和延迟范围。
• Fidelix表示赞赏，并期待该技术被整合到Moonlight等项目中。
• Superjan强调低延迟和低复杂度在某些应用中的重要性，而不仅仅关注压缩效率。
• Sitkack指出新视频编解码器的设计需要广泛的研究项目支持，以防止专利侵权。
• Nairoz好奇是否可以为特定游戏设计定制的视频编码器，优先编码重要区域。
• Kreco简单表达了对文章的感谢和欣赏。
• Crazygringo对硬件编码与GPU加速编码的效率提出疑问，并希望看到实际的基准测试。
• Hashtekar回顾了30年前在视频压缩技术上的工作，对当前技术的发展表示欣慰。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是软件实现的低延迟编码是否优于现有的硬件编码解决方案。
• 另一个讨论点是专利对创新的潜在阻碍，尤其是在游戏流媒体编码领域。
• 不同编解码器之间的比较，包括JPEG-XS和H.264/AVC，也是讨论的重要部分。
• 还探讨了定制编码器和特定游戏优化的可能性。

44714914.article_content:
Streaming gameplay from one machine to another over a network is a reasonably popular use case these days. These use cases demand very, very low latency. Every millisecond counts here. We need to:
Send controller input from machine A to B over network
B renders a frame on the GPU
B encodes the frame into a bitstream
B sends the result over a network to A
A decodes the bitstream
A displays image on screen
Dopamine is released in target brain
Every step in this chain adds latency and we want to minimize this as much as possible. The go-to solution here is GPU accelerated video compression using whatever codec you have available, usually H.264, HEVC or if you’re really fancy, AV1. Ideally, we want all of this to complete in roughly ~20 ms.
To make this use case work well, we have to strangle the codecs quite a bit. Modern video codecs love latency since it allows tricks like flexible rate control and B-frames. That is what allows these codecs to operate at ridiculous compression ratios, but we have to throw away most of these tricks now. Since the codec cannot add latency, and we’re working on a fixed bit-rate budget (the ethernet cable or WiFi antenna), we’re left with:
Hard-capped constant bit rate
There is no buffer that can soak up variable bit rate
Infinite GOP P-frames or intra-refresh
Either choice deals with packet loss differently
When game streaming, the expectation is that we have a lot of bandwidth available. Streaming locally on a LAN in particular, bandwidth is basically free. Gigabit ethernet is ancient technology and hundreds of megabits over WiFi is no problem either. This shifts priorities a little bit for me at least.
Back in my student days, I designed a very simple low-complexity video codec for my master thesis, and after fiddling with Vulkan video and PyroFling for a while, that old itch was scratched again.
I wanted to see what would happen if I designed a codec with laser focus on local streaming with the absolute lowest possible latency, what could go wrong?
Throwing out motion prediction – intra-only
This is the grug-brained approach to video, but it’s not as silly as it sounds. Bit-rates explode of course, but we gain:
Excellent error resilience
Even on local WiFi streaming to a handheld device, this does matter quite a lot, at least in my experience
Simplicity
Duh
Consistent quality
With CBR, video quality is heavily dependent on how good of a job motion estimation can do
Intra-only has use cases in digital cinema (motion JPEG2000) and more professionally oriented applications where these concerns are likely more important than squeezing bandwidth. We’re now working at 100+ Mbits/s instead of ~10-20 Mbit/s, so streaming over the internet is no longer feasible outside of peer-to-peer with fiber links. For reference, raw 1080p60 with 420 chroma subsampling is in the range of 1.5 Gbit/s, and it only gets worse from there.
Throwing out entropy coding
Entropy coding is an absolute nightmare for parallelization, which means encoding solely on the GPU with compute shaders becomes an extremely painful affair. Let’s just throw that out and see how far we get. Gotta go fast!
There are codecs in this domain too, but it’s getting very specialized at this point. In the professional broadcasting space, there are codecs designed to squeeze more video through existing infrastructure with “zero” lag and minimal hardware cost. My master thesis was about this, for example. A more consumer oriented example is VESA display stream compression (I’m not sure if it does entropy coding, but the compression ratios are small enough I doubt it). There isn’t much readily available software in this domain, it’s generally all implemented in tiny ASICs. If FFmpeg doesn’t support it, it doesn’t exist for mere mortals.
Discrete Wavelet Transforms
While modern codecs are all block-based Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) + a million hacks on top to make it good, there is an alternative that tried its best in the 90s to replace DCTs, but kinda failed in the end.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UGXeRx0Tic4
is a nice video explaining some of the lore. DWT-based compression has a niche today, but only in intra video compression. It’s a shame, because it’s quite elegant.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discrete_wavelet_transform
A graphics programmer will be familiar with this structure immediately, because this is just good old mip-maps with spice. Effectively, we downsample images, and also compute the “error” between the high-res picture and low-res picture. With signal processing lenses on, we can say it’s a critically sampled filter-bank. After processing N pixels, we obtain N / 2 low-pass and N / 2 high-pass pixels. The filters designed to do this are very particular (I really don’t know or care how they were made), but it’s basically just a basic convolution kernel, nothing too wild. The number of levels can vary but I chose 5 levels of decomposition.

data.title: Different Clocks
data.author: pppone
data.article_summary:
Ianto Cannon创建的时钟图形使用JavaScript生成可缩放矢量图形（SVG），源代码可自由使用和修改。每个时钟显示当前的协调世界时（UTC），包括以下几种样式：

1. **Binary**：方块显示Unix时间，即自1970年以来的秒数，以32位整数表示。
2. **Polygons**：多边形显示时间，格式为yy:M:w:d:h:mm:ss，其中M是月份，w是当月第几周，d是星期几。
3. **Blobs**：左起第一个blob显示每千年波峰移动一次，后续blob分别显示每年的波峰、每天的波峰、每小时的波峰、每分钟的波峰和每秒的波峰，最后一个blob综合了所有六种波。
4. **Peaks**：最高峰每千年从右向左移动一次，依次递减至每分钟移动一次。
5. **Waves**：与Peaks类似，但使用贝塞尔曲线而非锐边。

Ianto Cannon
's clock graphics
These clocks are generated as scalable vector graphics using JavaScript. Feel free to use and modify the source code.
Each clock displays the current Coordinated Universal Time (UTC):
Loading…
Binary
These squares show the Unix time, which is a 32-bit signed integer representing the number of seconds since 1970.
Polygons
These polygons show the time in the format yy:M:w:d:h:mm:ss, where M is the month, w is the week in the month, and d is the day of the week.

Blobs
The leftmost blob has a travelling wave that passes the top once per millennium.
The following blobs have waves that pass once per year, day, hour, minute, and second, respectively.
The final blob has all six of the above waves on it.
Peaks
The highest peak moves from right to left once per millenium, the next highest once per year, once per day, once per hour, and once per minute.
Waves
Similar to the peaks, but using Bézier curves instead of sharp edges.

44714223.article_summary:
Ianto Cannon创建的时钟图形使用JavaScript生成可缩放矢量图形（SVG），源代码可自由使用和修改。每个时钟显示当前的协调世界时（UTC），包括以下几种样式：

1. **Binary**：方块显示Unix时间，即自1970年以来的秒数，以32位整数表示。
2. **Polygons**：多边形显示时间，格式为yy:M:w:d:h:mm:ss，其中M是月份，w是当月第几周，d是星期几。
3. **Blobs**：左起第一个blob显示每千年波峰移动一次，后续blob分别显示每年的波峰、每天的波峰、每小时的波峰、每分钟的波峰和每秒的波峰，最后一个blob综合了所有六种波。
4. **Peaks**：最高峰每千年从右向左移动一次，依次递减至每分钟移动一次。
5. **Waves**：与Peaks类似，但使用贝塞尔曲线而非锐边。

© Ianto Cannon 2025年7月28日

data.title: Robot hand could harvest blackberries better than humans
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 美国阿肯色大学开发了一种用于采摘黑莓的机器人夹爪，旨在解决近年来农场劳动力短缺的问题。该设备由机械工程师Anthony Gunderman及其团队开发，采用软机器人技术，具有三个由柔软材料制成的“手指”，灵感来自郁金香的开放和闭合机制。夹爪的指尖装有力传感器，确保采摘黑莓时不损伤果实。研究团队通过测量专业采摘者的力量，确定了合适的采摘力度。尽管该机器人尚未部署到农场，但未来有望比人工采摘更高效、一致，并可能用于采摘其他柔软水果。此外，该技术还有潜力帮助行动受限的人。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器人采摘黑莓的技术可行性、实用性和经济性

不同观点：
• ortusdux：认为力反馈传感器应用于成熟度检测可能比用于训练更有价值，强调了采摘动作中的成熟度检查。
• helltone：对技术的实际应用持怀疑态度，指出实验室环境与现实世界的差距，以及对安全性、经济性和维护成本的考虑不足。
• liawsjt：质疑该软抓取器的独特性，认为视觉、运动规划和控制比抓取器设计更具挑战，并提到已有公司投入巨资研发类似技术。
• ugh123：指出文章中未提及机器人手是否能比人类更好地 harvest，且关键的视觉和定位技术尚未开发。
• dfltr、andylynch：通过讽刺和实例指出劳动力短缺问题，但对技术实现持保留态度。
• autoexec：认为虽然机器人潜力巨大，但现实中仍存在诸多问题和限制，其实现和经济性仍待解决。

• Fomite：关注经济性，质疑机器人能否以比人类更低的成本采摘黑莓。
• robswc：支持自动化技术的发展，认为应自动化枯燥/艰苦的工作。
• KevinMS：认为廉价劳动力消失后，这类技术会自然出现。
• hulitu：质疑“可能”的技术新闻，强调实际成果的重要性。

• 多个评论提到视觉和定位技术的关键性，认为这是机器人采摘技术实现的瓶颈之一。
• 劳动力短缺问题被提及，部分评论认为这是推动自动化技术发展的动力。

44714954.article_content:
Robot Hand Could Harvest Blackberries Better Than Humans
July 21, 2025
Photo by Chieko Hara
Mechanical engineer Anthony Gunderman holds a prototype of the robotic gripper for picking blackberries.
Fresh, frozen and processed berries are a multi-billion-dollar business in America. In Arkansas alone, fresh-market blackberries contribute $24.3 million each year to the state’s economy. But these delicate blackberries sold in clamshells at supermarkets must be picked by hand, and farm labor has been limited in recent years. A new berry-picking robot gripper developed at the U of A could give growers a high-tech replacement for limited labor availability.
The U.S patent was issued in April to the U of A for the invention “Soft Robotic Gripper for Berry Harvesting.” Technology Ventures, part of the Division of Research and Innovation, secured the patent.
The device was developed by Anthony Gunderman, at the time a Ph.D. student and now an assistant professor in U of A’s Department of Mechanical Engineering, with Yue Chen, a former U of A professor now at Georgia Tech, and Jeremy Collins, then a U of A undergraduate engineering student.
Inspired by Nature
The robotic gripper has three “fingers,” each made of a soft, pliable material. When a “tendon” — in this case a guitar string — is pulled, the fingers retract.
Building robots from pliable materials is known as soft robotics, an approach first used in the 1960s. When designing soft robots, developers often look to nature for models, a process known as biomimicry. For the berry-picking hand, the researchers were inspired by the design of a tulip.
The robotic gripper can harvest delicate blackberries. (Illustration colorized by Ross Maute based on a photo by Anthony Gunderman)
“I was inspired by the way a tulip flower opens and closes when the sunlight hits it,” Gunderman said.
On the tip of each finger is a force sensor, which makes sure the gripper can pluck the berry without crushing it. Roughly handled blackberries can be damaged at harvest or turn red after harvest, a condition called red drupelet reversion
.
Both are undesirable attributes for consumers. The USDA will also reject fresh blackberries with too much damage or too many red drupelets.
To determine the force needed to pick blackberries without damage,
the engineers worked with Andrea Myers, then a graduate student, and Renee Threlfall
, an associate professor in food science with the Arkansas Agricultural Experiment Station, the research arm of the U of A System’s statewide Division of Agriculture.
The team attached sensors to the fingertips of experienced blackberry pickers and measured how much force they applied while harvesting a berry.
Before the robot can be deployed on farms, the computer vision and positioning technologies that would let it find and reach for berries on the plant still need to be developed.
Today, heartier fruits like blueberries and pears are commonly harvested by machines. And rougher automated harvesting machines are used for blackberries that will be frozen or processed.
Better than a human
The human hand can adapt to many tasks. But Gunderman thinks one day the robotic hand could be better at picking blackberries.
“When we’re talking about one specific task, it is certainly the case that you could design something that is better than the human hand for that one specific task,” he said.
The robotic gripper could also be more consistent than human workers.
“Depending on if you have a brand-new hand harvester or someone who’s been doing it for decades, you will get vastly different berry quality,” Gunderman said.
The gripper could also be used to pick other soft fruits, such as raspberries.
The robotic gripper was tested on a range of objects, from hard items like a jar of pears and a can of beans to soft, flexible objects like a bag of potato chips and a T-shirt. The soft gripper, Gunderman said, might also be a tool for people with limited mobility due to injury or age.
Researchers measured the force needed to pick blackberries without damage. (Photo by Anthony Gunderman, University of Arkansas and University of Arkansas System Division of Agriculture)
About the University of Arkansas:
As Arkansas' flagship institution, the U of A provides an internationally competitive education in more than 200 academic programs. Founded in 1871, the U of A contributes more than
$3 billion to Arkansas’ economy
through the teaching of new knowledge and skills, entrepreneurship and job development, discovery through research and creative activity while also providing training for professional disciplines. The Carnegie Foundation classifies the U of A among the few U.S. colleges and universities with the highest level of research activity.
U.S. News & World Report
ranks the U of A among the top public universities in the nation. See how the U of A works to build a better world at
Arkansas Research and Economic Development News.

data.author: thebestmoshe

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Anthropic对Claude使用设置的周限制及其影响

不同观点：
• Wowfunhappy：对每周限制感到紧张，担心一旦达到限制，整个星期都无法使用已习惯的工具。他质疑Anthropic所说的5%用户受影响的声明，认为这个比例过高。
• Jimbo808：不喜欢使用有限资源的感觉，习惯于互联网和短信等不限量服务。认为当前的定价模式让人感觉不好。
• OtherShrezzing：认为Anthropic的邮件不够具体，无法判断自己是否在受限的5%用户中。对"5%"的定义表示怀疑，认为这可能涵盖了大多数活跃用户。
• Strictnein：对"Max 20x"和"Max 5x"计划的资源分配感到困惑，质疑为何"Max 20x"不是"Max 5x"的四倍，而仅是略多。
• Alwillis：引用Anthropic的Reddit账号，提到一个用户在$200的套餐中消耗了数万美元的模型使用量。认为新限制是为了确保公平和防止账户共享及转售。
• Serf：认为$200的月套餐不够，需要一个不受时间限制和强制休息的方案。对"35小时"的限制表示不满，认为这在实际使用中根本不够。
• Submeta：认为Anthropic的解释模糊，缺乏对使用量的透明度。质疑Anthropic是否真的在针对滥用用户，还是只是为了限制访问找借口。
• Rstupek：认为"24/7运行Claude"的用户导致了限制措施，对这种行为表示不满。
• Wg0：认为滥用问题确实存在，但AI公司更多是受贪婪驱动，等待高估值收购。
• Jjcm：认为应该采用计量收费方案，而不是固定费用计划。指出AI公司正在调整限制以应对极端用户，但这导致了用户对价格的更多关注。
• Data-ottawa：认为5%的限制比例过高，质疑这是基于用户数量的任意削减。对新功能（如子代理）是否增加使用量表示担忧。
• Steve_adams_86：自认为在95%不受限的用户中，对那些轻易达到限制的用户行为感到好奇，并认为一些时间远离工具反而有助于保持思路清晰。
• Neom：正在开发一个编码代理，征求其他开发者对定价和可预测性的意见，担心复杂的信用系统不被用户接受。
• Swalsh：要求明确显示使用限制和已用量，以便用户清楚自己的使用情况。
• Sauwan：希望看到自己之前月份的使用情况，以判断是否会受到限制，对自己是否在5%中缺乏认知。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Anthropic对用户使用Claude设置的每周限制是否合理及其透明度问题。
• 用户对定价模式、限制的具体影响以及如何避免滥用行为存在不同看法。
• 一些用户对Anthropic的解释和沟通方式表示不满，认为缺乏具体细节和透明度。
• 部分用户对如何有效管理使用量和定价方案提出了自己的建议和看法。

• OtherShrezzing：认为Anthropic的邮件不够具体，无法判断自己是否在受限的5%用户中。对"5%"的定义表示怀疑，认为这可能涵盖了大多数活跃用户。
• Strictnein：对"Max 20x"和"Max 5x"计划的资源分配感到困惑，质疑为何"Max 20x"不是"Max 5x"的四倍，而仅是略多。
• Alwillis：引用Anthropic的Reddit账号，提到一个用户在$200的套餐中消耗了数万美元的模型使用量。认为新限制是为了确保公平和防止账户共享及转售。
• Serf：认为$200的月套餐不够，需要一个不受时间限制和强制休息的方案。对"35小时"的限制表示不满，认为这在实际使用中根本不够。
• Submeta：认为Anthropic的解释模糊，缺乏对使用量的透明度。质疑Anthropic是否真的在针对滥用用户，还是只是为了限制访问找借口。
• Rstupek：认为"24/7运行Claude"的用户导致了限制措施，对这种行为表示不满。
• Wg0：认为滥用问题确实存在，但AI公司更多是受贪婪驱动，等待高估值收购。
• Jjcm：认为应该采用计量收费方案，而不是固定费用计划。指出AI公司正在调整限制以应对极端用户，但这导致了用户对价格的更多关注。
• Data-ottawa：认为5%的限制比例过高，质疑这是基于用户数量的任意削减。对新功能（如子代理）是否增加使用量表示担忧。
• Steve_adams_86：自认为在95%不受限的用户中，对那些轻易达到限制的用户行为感到好奇，并认为一些时间远离工具反而有助于保持思路清晰。
• Neom：正在开发一个编码代理，征求其他开发者对定价和可预测性的意见，担心复杂的信用系统不被用户接受。
• Swalsh：要求明确显示使用限制和已用量，以便用户清楚自己的使用情况。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Anthropic对用户使用Claude设置的每周限制是否合理及其透明度问题。
• 用户对定价模式、限制的具体影响以及如何避免滥用行为存在不同看法。
• 一些用户对Anthropic的解释和沟通方式表示不满，认为缺乏具体细节和透明度。
• 部分用户对如何有效管理使用量和定价方案提出了自己的建议和看法。

data.title: Sign in with Google in Chrome
data.author: frizlab
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了在使用不同浏览器访问如Yelp等网站时遇到的"使用Google登录"提示问题。在Safari和Firefox中，这些提示会频繁出现，但Google Chrome中不会显示。通过在Safari中模拟Chrome的User-Agent，可以避免看到这些提示。然而，Chrome自身会有一个独特的One Tap对话框提示，这是浏览器原生界面的一部分，无法通过扩展如StopTheMadness Pro隐藏。用户可以在Chrome设置中通过输入特定地址（chrome://settings/content/federatedIdentityApi）并选择“阻止身份服务登录提示”来禁用此对话框。文章最后指出，这是Google通过Chrome获得优势的又一个例子。

44715166.article_content:
Sign in with Google in Chrome
July 28, 2025
By Jeff Johnson of
Underpass App Company
Many websites such as Yelp show an annoying âSign in with Googleâ banner when you visit.
This is what Google calls
the One Tap user experience
. Fortunately, my web browser extension
StopTheMadness Pro
hides âSign in with Googleâ banners.
What you may not realize if you use Safari or Firefox is that the banners are never displayed in Google Chrome! You can see this in macOS Safari by spoofing the Chrome User-Agent header. In Safari Advanced Settings, enable âShow features for web developers.â This setting adds a Develop menu to Safariâs main menu bar. The Develop menu includes a User Agent submenu with a list of several web browsers. When you select Google Chrome from the list and then load Yelp, the âSign in with Googleâ banners no longer appear in Safari.
Although Chrome avoids the âSign in with Googleâ banners, Googleâs browser still has its own custom annoyance. If youâre already signed in to your Google account when you visit a participating website such as Yelp, Chrome will display a One Tap dialog.
This dialog differs from the âSign in with Googleâ banners you see in Safari and Firefox in a couple of important ways. First, the Chrome dialog is
not
an element in the web page but rather a part of the Chrome native app user interface. Thus, StopTheMadness Pro cannot hide the dialog. Indeed, while Chrome is displaying the dialog, it blocks
all
Chrome extension popup windows from appearing. Selecting an extension in the Extensions toolbar widget does nothing. (In other words, itâs not a bug in StopTheMadness Pro.)
The second difference is that the Chrome dialog can be disabled in Chromeâs Settings. Enter
chrome://settings/content/federatedIdentityApi
in the address bar to access the setting directly.
Select âBlock sign-in prompts from identity servicesâ to stop the dialogs from appearing in Chrome.
If the courts and antitrust regulators are reading—they probably wonât read my blog, but one can dream—this is yet another example of Google advantaging its own browser Chrome over other web browsers.

data.title: SQLx – Rust SQL Toolkit
data.author: stmw
data.article_summary: SQLx 是一个用于 Rust 的异步 SQL 工具包，支持 PostgreSQL、MySQL、MariaDB 和 SQLite，强调纯 Rust 实现和运行时无关性。它具有编译时检查查询功能，不使用 DSL。SQLx 提供连接池、行流式处理、自动语句准备和缓存，以及嵌套事务等特性。对于 TLS 支持，SQLx 可与多种运行时（如 tokio、async-std）和 TLS 后端（如 native-tls、rustls）集成。使用时需根据选择的运行时和 TLS 需求在 `Cargo.toml` 中添加相应特性。SQLx 并非 ORM，且自 0.7 版本起移除了 MSSQL 支持，计划在 SQLx Pro 项目中重写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕SQL工具和ORM库的优缺点，特别是在处理动态查询、类型安全、异步操作和不同编程语言中的数据库操作方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持SQLx的观点**：
   - **[Ameo]**：认为SQLx是Rust中处理数据库的最佳选择，尤其喜欢其编译时检查和迁移系统，相比其他ORM（如Diesel和sea-orm）更加好用。
   - **[mcflubbins]**：使用过SQLx，认为其最大优势是编译时检查查询，虽然需要一定的适应时间。
   - **[chuckhend]**：喜欢SQLx，正在寻找在Python或JS项目中实现类似编译时检查的方法。

• **对SQLx的批评和问题**：
   - **[tmpfs]**：认为SQLx难以抽象底层数据库，特别是在Docker化时需要在编译时运行PostgreSQL，增加了复杂性，因此转用其他库如sqlite和postgres。
   - **[lsuresh]**：最初以为SQLx像JOOQ（Java中的SQL工具），但发现其较为低级，没有很好地抽象底层数据库，且类型转换存在问题，因此改用rust-postgres。
   - **[moggers123]**：希望SQLx有非异步接口，因异步操作导致项目延迟大幅增加，最终改用rusqlite。
   - **[thesuperbigfrog]**：在使用SQLx与SQLite时遇到连接池问题，导致数据库意外断开，最终改用NoSQL方案解决问题。

• **对动态查询构建的关注**：
   - **[banashark]**：指出纯SQL方法在处理动态查询构建（如条件连接、选择、过滤等）时容易变得混乱，Kysely在这方面做得不错，但最终很多开发者会选择ORM来解决复杂问题。

• **对其他工具的偏好**：
   - **[germandiago]**：习惯使用C++和sqlpp11，认为其通过生成代码提供编译时检查和代码补全功能。
   - **[owlstuffing]**：提到Manifold-sql在Java中的集成优于SQLx在Rust中的集成，特别是在类型安全和编译时检查方面。
   - **[nbf_1995]**：认为SQLx和F#的类型提供器在编写数据库访问代码方面提供了极好的开发体验。

• **对SQLx处理复杂查询的批评**：
   - **[karlmdavis]**：认为SQLx在处理数据库连接查询时非常困难，最终转用Diesel，尽管Diesel也有问题，但能避免一些糟糕的hack手段。

补充讨论：
• **异步操作的争议**：SQLx的异步操作在某些情况下会导致性能问题，特别是高并发或高负载环境下，部分开发者因此放弃使用SQLx。
• **SQL与ORM的取舍**：部分开发者认为纯SQL方法虽然灵活但难以处理复杂动态查询，而ORM可以简化这些问题，但也带来其他复杂性。
• **跨语言比较**：讨论中提到了多种语言（Rust、C++、Java、F#）中的SQL工具和ORM库，展示了不同语言生态中开发者对SQL工具的不同需求和偏好。

争议焦点：SQLx的异步特性及其在处理复杂查询和连接时的表现是主要争议点。部分开发者认为其编译时检查是巨大优势，而另一些开发者则因其实现复杂性和性能问题而转向其他工具。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对"Shrinkle"游戏的反馈与建议

data.title: Interstellar Comet 3I/Atlas: What We Know Now
data.author: bikenaga
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕发现及观察星际彗星3I/ATLAS的科学分析与未来可能性

不同观点：
• Fripplebubby：通过概率方法推断彗星大小。他认为，基于观测数据，彗星大小可能在10公里或0.5公里之间，但由于多年来对彗星的观察经验，看到一个大彗星的概率极低，因为根据幂律分布，我们应该会看到更多小彗星。因此，可以推断该彗星更可能是0.5公里大小。
• NitpickLawyer：强调Vera Rubin天文台的重要性，认为其在发现彗星3I前的10天已经拍摄到该物体，这对调整和验证其模型非常有价值。此外，他对未来Rubin天文台的发现充满期待，并指出多个天文台的联合观测将提供大量数据。
• drewg123：提到Rubin的观测显示彗星尾部朝向太阳，而不是远离太阳，这与通常的彗星行为不同，并开玩笑地提出是否是减速燃烧。

补充讨论：
• gnabgib：提供了与3I/ATLAS相关的其他讨论链接，包括其他天文台的观察和与该彗星相关的科学研究，显示出该发现引起了广泛的科学兴趣。
• EspadaV9：提出未来可能利用探测器搭乘星际物体，以实现更快速的星际旅行，类似于Voyager 1但速度更快。
• supportengineer：简单提及受讨论启发，打算重温电影《不要抬头》。
• unsupp0rted：幽默地提出一种假设，即如果星际物体被观察，是否意味着“居民在扫描我们”，虽然自知不太可能。

争议焦点：
• 彗星尾部朝向太阳这一异常现象引发了讨论，drewg123提出的“减速燃烧”虽然是玩笑，但反映了科学界对异常现象的关注和探讨。

总结：
讨论围绕彗星3I/ATLAS的发现、观测方法、科学价值及未来探测可能性展开。不同观点集中在彗星大小的推断方法、观测数据的科学价值以及未来星际探测的设想，同时对彗星异常现象提出了幽默的解释和探讨。

data.title: Visa and Mastercard are getting overwhelmed by gamer fury over censorship
data.author: mrzool
data.article_summary: 游戏玩家不满Steam和itch.io下架成人游戏，将愤怒转向支付处理公司Visa和Mastercard，发起大规模邮件和电话抗议活动。玩家认为这些支付公司是下架的幕后推手，尽管其规则模糊。玩家在社交媒体上组织动员，通过打电话和发邮件施压，意图通过制造沟通障碍，迫使支付公司关注问题。尽管客服代表表示无权改变政策，玩家仍坚持通过占用线路和回拨占用其他客户的服务资源。玩家还向高管发送邮件，并保持礼貌态度以增加影响力。同时，有组织提供资源和脚本帮助玩家参与抗议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：支付处理公司作为 gatekeeper 对内容进行审查的争议

不同观点：
• Kapura：认为少数人基于个人喜恶推动审查是荒谬的，特别是当这些内容并没有强迫任何人消费时。主张应继续对支付处理公司施压，同时也需抵制那些试图决定其他成年人如何支配时间的人。
• numpad0：指出最初被下架的是色情内容，但现在审查范围已扩展到恐怖游戏，如《Mouthwashing(2024)》。担忧审查范围会继续扩大。
• duxup：批评支付处理系统的不透明性，举例一家制作剑的公司无故被禁止使用信用卡支付，且无法得知具体原因或申诉。
• benoau：引用Collective Shout的博客，指出当Steam未回应时，他们转向支付处理公司施压，认为这是有效的策略。
• ThrowawayR2：认为消费者和企业对Visa、Mastercard没有其他选择，主张应向政治人物施压，特别是民主党立法者，以获得支持和选票。
• dehugger：建议Steam改变政策，让成人游戏只能用商店信用购买，以解决支付处理问题。
• tflinton：提醒大家即使某些内容不违法，也可能带来民事问题和风险，支付处理公司可能不得不采取审查措施以规避风险。
• motbus3：感叹当今社会人人想当审查者或统治者，表达对此趋势的不满。
• SilverElfin：认为某些内容应受到严格监管，但私人支付应由政府作为公共服务提供，以避免审查。
• vunderba：提供一个相关的在线请愿链接，呼吁对支付处理公司施压。
• bsenftner：质疑相关文章的真实性，认为其迎合游戏观众，没有实质内容。
• nemomarx：提供信息称Collective Shout通过大量电话成功引起支付公司注意，建议继续保持这种压力。
• 3acctforcom：认为普通人的电话无法影响大公司高层的决策，强调权力运作的现实。
• scirob：询问是否有任何行动可以减少这些公司的权力。
• CivBase：对“玩家愤怒”能否带来实质性改变持怀疑态度，但承认当前的Stop Killing Games活动可能具有一定影响力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于支付处理公司作为gatekeeper审查内容的合理性和合法性，以及应如何有效抵制这种趋势。
• 讨论中涉及的具体案例（如《Mouthwashing(2024)》游戏和制作剑的公司）突显了审查对不同类型内容的影响。
• 建议的应对策略包括向支付处理公司施压、通过政治途径寻求改变、以及利用集体行动引起注意。
• 对当前审查系统的透明度和申诉机制缺失的问题也有较多批评。

News
Visa and Mastercard are getting overwhelmed by gamer fury over censorship
Gamers are sending mass emails and phone calls to major payment processors in protest over Steam and itch.io
by
Patricia Hernandez
Jul 28, 2025, 4:06 PM UTC
Facebook
Link
Image: OppaiMan
In the wake of storefronts
like Steam and itch.io curbing the sale of adult games
, irate fans have started an organized campaign against the payment processors that they believe are responsible for the crackdown. While the movement is still in its early stages, people are mobilizing with an eye toward overwhelming communication lines at companies like Visa and Mastercard in a way that will make the concern impossible to ignore.
On social media sites like Reddit and Bluesky, people are urging one another to get into contact with Visa and Mastercard through emails and phone calls. Visa and Mastercard have become the targets of interest because
the affected storefronts
both say that their decisions around adult games were motivated by the danger of losing the ability to use major payment processors while selling games. These payment processors have their own rules regarding usage, but they are vaguely defined. But losing infrastructure like this could impact audiences well beyond those who care about sex games, spokespeople for Valve and itch.io said.
In a now-deleted post on the Steam subreddit with over 17,000 upvotes
, commenters say that customer service representatives for both payment processors seem to already be aware of the problem. Sometimes, the representatives will say that they’ve gotten multiple calls on the subject of adult game censorship, but that they can’t really do anything about it.
The folks applying pressure know that someone at a call center has limited power in a scenario like this one; typically, agents are equipped to handle standard customer issues like payment fraud or credit card loss. But the point isn’t to enact change through a specific phone call: It’s to cause enough disruption that the ruckus theoretically starts costing payment processors money.
“Emails can be ignored, but a very very long queue making it near impossible for other clients to get in will help a lot as well,” reads the top comment on the Reddit thread. In that same thread, people say that they’re hanging onto the call even if the operator says that they’ll experience multi-hour wait times presumably caused by similar calls gunking up the lines. Beyond the stubbornness factor, the tactic is motivated by the knowledge that most customer service systems will put people who opt for call-backs in a lower priority queue, as anyone who opts in likely doesn’t have an emergency going on.
Image: OppaiMan
“Do both,” one commenter suggests. “Get the call back, to gum up the call back queue. Then call in again and wait to gum up the live queue.”
People are also using email to voice their concerns directly to the executives at both Visa and Mastercard, payment processors that activist group Collective Shout called out by name in their open letter requesting that adult games get pulled. Emails are also getting sent to customer service. In light of the coordinated effort, many people are getting a pre-written response that reads:
Thank you for reaching out and sharing your perspective. As a global company, we follow the laws and regulations everywhere we do business. While we explicitly prohibit illegal activity on our network, we are equally committed to protecting legal commerce. If a transaction is legal, our policy is to process the transaction. We do not make moral judgments on legal purchases made by consumers. Visa does not moderate content sold by merchants, nor do we have visibility into the specific goods or services sold when we process a transaction. When a legally operating merchant faces an elevated risk of illegal activity, we require enhanced safeguards for the banks supporting those merchants. For more information on Visa’s policies, please visit our network integrity page on Visa.com. Thank you for writing.
On platforms like Bluesky, resources are being shared to help people know who to contact and how, including possible scripts for talking to representatives or sending emails. A website has been set up with the explicit purpose of arming concerned onlookers with the tools and knowledge necessary to do their part in the campaign.
Through it all, gamers are telling one another to remain cordial during any interactions with payment processors, especially when dealing with low-level workers who are just trying to do their job. For executives, the purpose of maintaining a considerate tone is to help the people in power take the issue seriously.
The strategy is impressive in its depth and breadth of execution. While some charge in with an activist bent, others say that
they’re pretending to be confused customers
who want to know why they can’t use Visa or Mastercard to buy their favorite games.

data.title: Is SoftBank still backing OpenAI?
data.author: samuli
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了软银和OpenAI合作的"Stargate项目"存在的严重误导问题。最初宣布投资5000亿美元用于AI超级计算项目，但随后计划大幅缩减，仅计划在年底前建一个小型数据中心。文章指出，尽管媒体广泛报道了德州阿比林的数据中心与Stargate项目有关，但实际上该项目与软银无关，也未获得软银的资金支持。OpenAI和其CEO Sam Altman故意通过混淆视听的方式，使外界误以为软银深度参与了该项目。文章最后质疑OpenAI和软银的所有公开声明和承诺的可信度，认为其中可能存在更多误导信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI与特朗普政府宣布的5000亿美元Stargate项目的真实性与动机分析

不同观点：
• **怀疑和批评立场：**
  - [eightysixfour] 认为5000亿美元的Stargate项目从一开始就不是真实的，只是为了给一位专制总统政治上的胜利，同时转移注意力。虽然不喜欢这种做法，但也能理解企业的行为，将其与富士康的LCD工厂项目相提并论。
  - [sharadov] 强调这种大投资的宣布只是为了取悦特朗普及其支持者（MAGA群体），实际并无实质内容，所有举动只是为了制造“大交易”的假象。
  - [gsibble] 认为整个项目不过是营销上的障眼法，显得非常可悲。

• **理解和政治信号立场：**
  - [ashvardanian] 承认5000亿美元是一个吸引眼球的数字，但并不认为有人真的期待这个数字的准确性。该数字更多是政治意愿的信号，虽然大项目往往超出预期时间和成本，但OpenAI在融资方面仍有优势。

• **商业策略立场：**
  - [iFire] 提出在OpenAI仍有领导地位时出售股份并进行多样化投资是有道理的，从商业角度看待这一事件。

• **个人评价立场：**
  - [Havoc] 暗示Altman可能因为不够“疯狂”而被Strategic Bets（SB）排除在外，这是一种对个人能力的评价。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于5000亿美元项目的真实性与动机。一部分评论者认为这是政治作秀，另一部分则认为这是常见的商业和政治策略，且数字本身不具备实际意义，更多是象征性的。
- 评论中多次提到特朗普及其支持者对“大数字”和“大交易”的偏好，暗示这些项目主要是为了政治宣传。
- 对OpenAI及其融资能力的评价存在分歧，一部分人对其持批评态度，另一部分则认可其在资本运作上的优势。

44713945.article_content:
Is SoftBank Still Backing OpenAI?
Edward Zitron
Jul 24, 2025
37 min read
Earlier in the week,
the Wall Street Journal reported
that SoftBank and OpenAI's "$500 billion" "AI Project" was now setting a "more modest goal of building a small data center by year-end."
To quote:
A $500 billion effort unveiled
at the White House
to supercharge the U.S.’s artificial-intelligence ambitions has struggled to get off the ground and has sharply scaled back its near-term plans.
Six months after Japanese billionaire Masayoshi Son stood shoulder to shoulder with Sam Altman and President
Trump
to announce the Stargate project, the newly formed company charged with making it happen has yet to complete a single deal for a data center.
One might be forgiven for being a little confused here, as there is, apparently, a Stargate Data Center being built in Abilene Texas. Yet the Journal added another detail:
Altman has used the Stargate name, shared with a 1994 Kurt Russell film about aliens who teleport to ancient Egypt, on projects that aren’t being financed by the partnership between OpenAI and SoftBank. The trademark to Stargate is held by SoftBank, according to public filings.
For instance, OpenAI refers to a data center in Abilene, Texas, and another it agreed in March to use in Denton, Texas, as part of Stargate even though they are being done without SoftBank, some of the people familiar with the matter said.
Confusing, right? One might also be confused by the Bloomberg story called "
Inside The First Stargate AI Data Center
," which had the subheadline "OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank hope that the site in Texas is the first of many across the US." More-confusingly, the piece talked about Stargate LLC, which OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank were (allegedly) shareholders of.
Yet I have confirmed that SoftBank never, ever had any involvement with the site in Abilene Texas. It didn't fund it, it didn't build it, it didn't choose the site and, in fact, does not appear to have anything to do with
any
data center that OpenAI uses. The data center many, many reporters have referred to as "Stargate" has nothing to do with the "Stargate data center project."  Any reports suggesting otherwise are wrong, and I believe that this is a conscious attempt at misleading the public by OpenAI and SoftBank.
I confirmed the following with a PR representative from Crusoe, one of the developers of the site in Abilene Texas:
Funding for construction of [the] Abilene data center is a JV between Crusoe, Blue Owl and Primary Digital Infrastructure. Confirming that Softbank is not and has not been involved in the funding for its construction.
And, as a reminder,
Stargate as an entity was never formed
—
my source being the CEO of Oracle Safra Catz on Oracle’s earnings call
.
This is an astonishing — and egregious — act of misinformation on the part of Sam Altman and OpenAI. By my count,
at
least
15
different
stories attribute the Abilene Texas data center to the Stargate project, despite the fact that SoftBank was never and has never been involved. One would forgive anyone who got this wrong, because
OpenAI itself engaged in the deliberate deception in its own announcement of the Stargate Project
[emphasis mine]:
The initial equity funders in Stargate are SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX. SoftBank and OpenAI are the lead partners for Stargate, with SoftBank having financial responsibility and OpenAI having operational responsibility. Masayoshi Son will be the chairman.
Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are the key initial technology partners. The buildout is currently underway,
starting in Texas
, and we are evaluating potential sites across the country for more campuses as we finalize definitive agreements.
You can weasel-word all you want about how nobody has directly reported that SoftBank was or was not part of Abilene. This is a deliberate, intentional deception, perpetrated by OpenAI and SoftBank, who deliberately misled both the public and the press as a means of keeping up the appearance that SoftBank was deeply involved in (and financially obligated to) the Abilene site.
Based on reporting that existed at the time but was never drawn together, it appears that Abilene was earmarked
by Microsoft
for OpenAI's use as early as July 2024, and never involved SoftBank in any way, shape or form. The "Stargate" Project, as reported,
was over six months old when it was announced in January 2025, and there have been no additional sites added other than Abilene.
In simpler terms,
Stargate does not exist other than as a name that Sam Altman gives things to make them feel more special than they are, and SoftBank was never involved.
Stargate does not exist as reported.
The use of the term "Stargate" is an intentional act of deceit, but beneath the surface lies, in my mind, a much bigger story. Furthermore, I believe this deceit means that we should review any and all promises made by OpenAI and SoftBank, and reconsider any and all statements they've made,

data.title: Requesting Funding for 90s.dev
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: 文章作者介绍了一个名为90s.dev的项目，最初误称为“视频游戏制作工具”，但实际上是一个复古操作系统网页环境，计划在其中开发游戏制作功能。由于时间和资金限制，项目发布时尚未完成，作者为此寻求资助。由于需要维持生计，作者提出通过GitHub Sponsors按小时付费的方案：每收到25美元，就投入一小时开发90s.dev。该项目已经耗费作者大量时间和精力，且代码完全前端化，难以直接 monetize。作者提供了项目源码和文档链接，并邀请有兴趣的人通过GitHub Sponsors进行资助。
data.comments_summary:

#
Requesting funding for 90s.dev
Hi everyone. A couple months ago I posted 90s.dev under the wrong title.
I called it a video game maker, because that’s the
vision
I had for it.
But I posted it prematurely, and it wasn’t yet a video game maker.
It was
an retro os web environment
, which I planned to make a game maker
in
.
So a lot of you showed interest, but I asked you to come back later.
Well, the problem was that I need to be monetized for my efforts on it.
I have practically no spare time due to my state and duties in life.
I
want
to work on it, but I had to focus on making money.
I was able to work on it for 3 months because I burned through
all my savings
.
Plus it’s entirely front-end code, which is inherently hard to monetize.
This is the age old problem of how to fund open source.
So I had an idea that I thought might be a good solution.
I would use GitHub Sponsors, but as a way to pay me hourly.
Instead of tiers, you would just specify an amount,
and for each $25 that I receive, I would work one hour on 90s.dev.
Since this would essentially be employment, I should share my resume.
90s.dev
App source:
https://github.com/sdegutis/os.90s.dev
Docs source:
https://github.com/sdegutis/90s.dev
I spent about 3 months on it, working ~14 hours a day, 6-7 days a week
[1]
.
It was my first time learning about and using most web worker features.
I had to learn about threads, broadcast channels, message ports, etc.
(At one point it used a shared worker for the file system but I took it out.)
hram.dev
– my day job
Old portfolio
To help fund this open source project,
go to
https://github.com/sponsors/sdegutis
.
Thanks for reading this, and I hope you have a lovely day.
See
https://github.com/sdegutis/os.90s.dev/graphs/code-frequency
and
https://github.com/sdegutis/90s.dev/graphs/code-frequency

Back to Blog
News
Supply Chain Security Alert: num2words PyPI Package Shows Signs of Compromise
Popular Python Package num2words v0.5.15 Published Without Repository Tag, Linked to Known Threat Actor
Ashish Kurmi
View LinkedIn
July 28, 2025
Share on X
Share on X
Share on LinkedIn
Share on Facebook
Follow our RSS feed
Table of Contents
Loading nav...
Key Takeaways
The Python package num2words version 0.5.15 was published to PyPI without a corresponding tag in the official GitHub repository
Security researcher
@johnk3r
identified potential links to the "Scavenger" threat actor, known for previous supply chain attacks
PyPI has removed the compromised package, preventing further installations
This incident highlights the ongoing risks in the Python ecosystem's supply chain security
The Incident
On July 28, 2025, the Python community was alerted to a potential supply chain attack involving the popular num2words package. Version 0.5.15 of this widely-used library for converting numbers to words was published to PyPI approximately 2 hours before being flagged as potentially compromised.
â
PyPI release history showing the suspicious v0.5.15 release published "about 2 hours ago"
Red Flags and Initial Detection
The compromise was first identified through several concerning indicators:
Missing Repository Tag
: Unlike previous releases, version 0.5.15 was published to PyPI without a corresponding tag in the official GitHub repository at
https://github.com/savoirfairelinux/num2words/tags
Timing Discrepancy
: The package appeared on PyPI without any associated commits or release activities in the source repository
Community Alert
: Security researcher @johnk3r quickly raised the alarm on social media, warning the community about potential compromise
GitHub repository tags showing the absence of v0.5.15, while previous versions (v0.5.14, v0.5.13, etc.) all have corresponding tags
The Scavenger Connection
According to @johnk3r's analysis, early indicators suggest this incident may be linked to "Scavenger," a threat actor previously associated with software supply chain intrusions. While full attribution requires deeper investigation, the modus operandi matches previous attacks:
Publishing malicious versions of legitimate packages
Exploiting the trust users place in established package names
Targeting popular packages to maximize potential impact
https://x.com/johnk3r/status/1949862337340461528
Credit:
https://x.com/johnk3r/status/1949862337340461528/photo/1
Automated Tools Already Upgrading to Malicious Version
Despite the quick response, automated dependency management tools had already begun creating pull requests to upgrade projects to the compromised version. A GitHub search reveals numerous automated PRs attempting to update num2words to version 0.5.15, demonstrating how quickly malicious packages can propagate through the ecosystem. Here is a sample pull request:
https://github.com/tarcisio-sousa/agiliza/pull/1075
Impact and Response
The num2words package is a widely-used Python library that provides functionality to convert numbers into their word representations across multiple languages. With thousands of downloads daily, any compromise could have had significant reach across the Python ecosystem.
Fortunately, the rapid response from the community and PyPI administrators helped contain the potential damage:
Quick Detection
: The suspicious release was identified within hours of publication
Swift Action
: PyPI removed the compromised package, preventing new installations
Community Warning
: Security alerts spread quickly through social media and developer channels
What You Should Do
If you use num2words in your projects:
Check Your Environment
â
Run
pip list | grep num2words
to verify which version you have installed
â
Downgrade if Necessary
f you have v0.5.15 installed, immediately downgrade to v0.5.14 using
pip install num2words==0.5.14
â
Audit Your Systems
Review logs and systems that may have installed the compromised version
â
Update Security Practices
Consider implementing additional supply chain security measures

data.title: What Happened When Hitler Took on Germany's Central Banker
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了希特勒上台初期试图控制德国央行（Reichsbank）的努力，以及时任央行行长汉斯·路德（Hans Luther）如何抵制这些压力。1933年1月30日，希特勒就任总理数小时后，纳粹冲锋队强行进入央行并升起纳粹旗帜，路德立即向希特勒抗议，强调央行是独立机构，最终纳粹旗帜被撤下。希特勒试图逼迫路德辞职，但由于央行受1924年法律保护，其行长由包括国际银行家在内的14人董事会任命，希特勒无法直接将其撤职。路德凭借其丰富的政治和经济经验，以及在金融危机中的出色表现，成功保住了职位。文章还提到希特勒通过大规模清洗魏玛共和国公务员以巩固权力，但在此过程中无法撼动路德在央行的地位。

• southernplaces7详细描述了希特勒与时任央行行长之间的冲突，指出尽管央行行长最初拒绝希特勒的要求并主张法律保护央行的独立性，但最终在不到两个月内辞职，且被替换为希特勒的追随者。他批评标题所暗示的对抗并不真实存在，实际上的抵抗非常有限。
